answer: Pay rewards as nectar that only matures after the earner spends it: a new identity's credits stay locked until it has bought services from several unrelated established providers, each purchase leaving a public mirror of the transaction. A sybil farm can mint identities, but it cannot mature their nectar without paying real outsiders, which costs more than the mint is worth. Self-dealing loops give themselves away: their spend graph closes into a tight reef with no outside edges, so the network refuses to mature those credits and the farm's effort rots unspent.
